summary: Madhya Pradesh High Court granted anticipatory bail to Anil Rai, holding that caste-based abuse not in public view doesn't bar bail under SC/ST Act.

ground_truth.judgment_reason: The Court held that since the offence under the SC/ST Act was not prima facie committed in public view, there was no statutory bar on granting anticipatory bail. Bail was allowed with standard conditions.

defence_arguments: Whether bail can be granted when the accused is not the complainant or witness in the false FIR and is not directly linked to the extortion demand.

ground_truth.outcome_detail: Juvenile granted bail as prior cases were close in time, and no material showed likely criminal influence upon release

Witnesses and the deceased’s own complaints indicated harassment and extortion threats from the police. The applicant was arrested in November 2020 and remained in custody until bail was granted.
prosecution_arguments: Whether prolonged incarceration exceeding one-third of maximum sentence entitles first-time offender to bail under Section 479 BNSS 2023
defence_arguments: despite serious charges including abetment of suicide and extortion.
legal_principles: Section 479 BNSS 2023 mandates bail for first-time offenders after one-third of maximum sentence in custody
Prolonged pre-trial detention violates Article 21 of the Constitution
Courts must balance seriousness of offence with fundamental right to liberty
Bail can be granted despite serious charges if trial is delayed and statutory bail conditions are met
summary: Allahabad High Court granted bail to Devendra Shukla after nearly four years of custody, applying BNSS provisions for prolonged detention of first-time undertrials despite serious charges of extortion and abetment of suicide.

ground_truth.judgment_reason: The Court observed that although serious allegations existed, the applicant had spent over three years and nine months in jail without trial commencing. Citing the Supreme Court's directive in Re-Inhuman Conditions in 1382 Prisons, the Court applied Section 479 BNSS 2023, which mandates release of undertrial first-time offenders detained for over one-third of the maximum sentence.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Regular bail granted after nearly four years in custody, applying Supreme Court ruling on Section 479 BNSS 2023 for first-time offenders having undergone over one-third of maximum sentence

Live-in relationships require careful scrutiny before inferring lack of consent
Completed investigation and absence of flight risk support bail grant

ground_truth.outcome_detail: Anticipatory bail granted in a domestic violence related case considering absence of injury reports and petitioner’s age and status

case_title: 395/120B/412 Of The Indian Penal Code vs In Re: Amarendra Kumar Singh @ Amar Singh
charge_sheet: Amarendra Kumar Singh was accused of conspiring and participating in a robbery at the office of a finance company. He was in custody for over two years and three months. prosecution_arguments: Whether continued detention is justified when trial is delayed
and the accused was not present at the crime scene.
defence_arguments: co-accused are being tried separately
summary: Calcutta High Court granted regular bail to Amarendra Kumar Singh after over two years of custody in a robbery case, citing trial delays and his absence at the crime scene.

accused_profile.name: Amarendra Kumar Singh @ Amar Singh @ Pahalwan

ground_truth.judgment_reason: The court noted the prolonged detention, trial delay, and absence of the accused at the crime scene. It concluded that further detention was not warranted and granted bail subject to strict conditions to ensure presence and prevent tampering.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Regular bail granted after over two years in custody; court cited prolonged trial delay, absence at crime scene, and earlier liberty from Supreme Court to reapply for bail.

case_title: Mukeshbhai Vrujlal Maheta vs State Of Gujarat
charge_sheet: Mukeshbhai Vrujlal Maheta was arrested in August 2019 after police recovered 375.054 kg of poppy straw from his shop and adjoining godown in Junagadh. His multiple bail applications were earlier rejected. The present application was based on prolonged incarceration and medical grounds including cardiac disease and diabetes, along with trial delay. The prosecution argued medical care was provided in jail and trial was actively progressing.
prosecution_arguments: Whether prolonged incarceration and medical ailments can justify bail in a commercial quantity NDPS case when the statutory twin conditions under Section 37 are not satisfied.
legal_principles: Section 37 NDPS Act imposes stringent twin conditions for bail in commercial quantity cases
Medical treatment within jail custody does not automatically justify bail
Delay in trial must be evaluated along with reasons such as pandemic disruption
summary: Gujarat High Court rejected second successive bail plea of Mukeshbhai Maheta in a 375 kg poppy straw case under NDPS Act, citing lack of change in circumstances and statutory bar under Section 37.

ground_truth.judgment_reason: The Court held that Section 37 NDPS Act requires satisfaction of non-guilt and low likelihood of reoffending, which was not met in this case involving commercial quantity. Despite health concerns and trial delay, no substantial change in circumstances was shown. The delay was partly attributable to the COVID-19 pandemic, and trial had begun.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Second successive regular bail rejected under NDPS Act; court found no change in circumstance and cited large quantity (375.054 kg) of poppy straw seized

ground_truth.outcome_detail: Regular bail granted as no overt acts or recoveries were attributed to petitioner, who was allegedly used to open accounts for cyber fraud

ground_truth.outcome_detail: Regular bail granted after prolonged custody, submission of charge sheet, and parity with co-accused already granted bail

case_title: Karthik @ Ullalu Karthik vs Commissioner Of Police
charge_sheet: Karthik @ Ullalu Karthik was preventively detained under the Karnataka Goondas Act based on allegations of multiple criminal activities including murder, extortion, and ganja sale. The Advisory Board confirmed the detention, but the petitioner’s representation dated 12.01.2021 was not considered by the State Government or Advisory Board. The High Court found this to be a violation of constitutional safeguards.
prosecution_arguments: Whether preventive detention under the Goondas Act can be sustained when the detenu's representation was not considered by the State Government or Advisory Board
defence_arguments: violating Article 22(5) of the Constitution.
legal_principles: Failure to consider detenu's representation violates Article 22(5)
Both Advisory Board and State must consider representation independently
Preventive detention orders are void if constitutional safeguards are breached
summary: Karnataka High Court quashed the preventive detention of Karthik under the Goondas Act, ruling that his constitutional right to have his representation considered was violated.

ground_truth.judgment_reason: The court held that non-consideration of the detenu’s representation violated his fundamental right under Article 22(5). It emphasized that both the State Government and Advisory Board have independent constitutional duties to consider such representations, and their failure rendered the detention order illegal.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Preventive detention under Karnataka Goondas Act quashed due to non-consideration of representation by State and Advisory Board

case_title: Mohan Rajak vs The State Of Jharkhand

no antecedents exist
and co-accused have been granted bail.
summary: Cybercrime accused granted bail due to lack of antecedents and parity with co-accused.

case_title: Renukuntla Sravani vs The State Of Telangana
charge_sheet: Renukuntla Pramod Kumar was detained under preventive detention laws on grounds of involvement in four 2018 criminal cases involving attempt to murder, cheating, trespass, and extortion. The State claimed his actions created public fear, but he remained in judicial custody when the detention order was issued. His wife challenged the legality of the detention.
prosecution_arguments: Whether preventive detention is justified under 'public order' when the accused is already in custody and the alleged crimes can be prosecuted under regular criminal law.
legal_principles: Preventive detention should only apply where public order, not just law and order, is affected
Preventive laws are exceptional and cannot substitute criminal trial process
Detention orders must be supported by substantive reasoning and not issued mechanically
summary: Telangana High Court quashed the preventive detention of Renukuntla Pramod Kumar, ruling that the alleged offenses were law and order issues, not public order disturbances.

ground_truth.judgment_reason: The court held that the alleged crimes, though serious, did not amount to a disturbance of public order as defined constitutionally. It found the detention order to be mechanical, unsupported by proper reasoning, and an overreach of preventive detention powers.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Preventive detention quashed; accused to be released unless required in other criminal cases

case_title: Kalamuddin Ansari @ Doka vs State Of U.P.

ground_truth.judgment_reason: The court considered the absence of direct allegations, non-recovery of the child from the applicant, and the fact that co-accused with stronger roles were already granted bail. The applicant had no criminal history and had been in custody since January 2021.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Bail granted as the applicant was not named in FIR, no recovery was made from him, and co-accused with stronger allegations were already granted bail

case_title: Md. Aamir Ansari @ Rock vs The State Of Jharkhand

case_title: Kolindar Singh @ Kolindra vs State Of U.P.

defence_arguments: Whether the husband and father-in-law can be granted bail in a dowry death case where the deceased's dying declaration implicates them; applicability of presumption under Section 113B of the Evidence Act

The burden was on the husband to explain the incident, which he failed to do. No grounds were found to distinguish the applicants' case from co-accused whose bail was already rejected.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Bail rejected in dowry death case based on dying declaration implicating husband and in-laws; court found no grounds to distinguish case from previously rejected co-accused

ground_truth.outcome_detail: Bail granted as applicant was not named in FIR and her alleged role was limited to procuring clothes of the victim child for ritual purposes; co-accused with similar or greater role was already granted bail

case_title: Sumit Kumar vs State Of Delhi

ground_truth.judgment_reason: The Court held that since the petitioner was nearly 18, was being tried as an adult, and had committed a heinous offence while on bail in another serious case, the risk of reoffending and influencing witnesses was too high to justify release.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Regular bail rejected as the petitioner was tried as an adult for a heinous, premeditated murder and robbery while on bail in a previous case; risk of reoffending and witness tampering cited

case_title: Amit Ranjan vs Narcotics Control Bureau, Delhi

case_title: Naresh Mahato vs State Of Nct Of Delhi

His arrest from the hotel room and corroborating evidence made out a strong prima facie case. Given the serious nature of the offense and pending trial, bail was denied.
ground_truth.outcome_detail: Regular bail rejected as court found applicant was part of criminal conspiracy to extort money using fake ED summons, with corroborating CCTV and CDR evidence

summary: Bail was denied to Vinay Kumar Mishra for transporting 349 kg of ganja, as the court held that statutory bail conditions under Section 37 NDPS Act were not satisfied.

case_title: Smt. Mangeethadevi vs State
